issues.title: Test file not co-located with component
issues.description: The rule requires test files to be in the same directory as component files. The test file flow-icon-text.test.tsx was moved to a __tests__ subdirectory instead of being co-located with flow-icon-text.tsx in the same directory.
issues.rule_name: React Component Test Files Must Be Co-Located

issues.title: QueryClient instance mismatch between router context and provider
issues.description: The Storybook decorator creates a QueryClient instance mismatch. The `createTestRouter` function instantiates a new QueryClient (`new QueryClient()`) and passes it to the router context on line 32. However, the decorator wraps the component with `QueryClientProvider` using the module-level `queryClient` instance on line 43. This creates two separate QueryClient instances - one for the router context and one for the provider. Queries executed within the router tree will use a different cache than queries executed through the provider, causing cache inconsistency and potential state synchronization issues. The router and provider should share the same QueryClient instance.

issues.title: Missing Suspense fallback causes blank UI during loading
issues.description: The FlowIconText component wraps FlowIconTextImplementation in a Suspense boundary but doesn't provide a fallback prop. When the component suspends while fetching flow data via useSuspenseQuery, React has no fallback content to display, resulting in a blank space in the UI until the query resolves. This creates a poor user experience with no loading indicator. The original implementation should have included a fallback prop like `<Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />` to show a loading state during data fetching.

issues.title: Unused import violates Rule #12 noUnusedImports configuration
issues.description: The flow-icon-text.tsx file imports Skeleton from '@/components/ui/skeleton' on line 6 but never uses it in the component code. This directly violates Rule #12 'Unused Imports Must Be Automatically Removed' from AGENTS.md, which requires that unused imports be eliminated via automated linting. The biome.json configuration explicitly sets noUnusedImports as an error, meaning this should have been caught by pre-commit hooks. The unused import increases bundle size unnecessarily and indicates the linting process was bypassed or failed.

issues.title: Unused import: Skeleton
issues.description: `Skeleton` is imported but never used in this file, which violates the rule requiring unused imports to be removed.
issues.rule_name: Unused Imports Must Be Automatically Removed

findings.title: Component ships with no tests despite checklist claim
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/`, the PR claims a `flow-icon-text.test.tsx` with MSW-mocked API tests, but the file is missing. Add it next to `flow-icon-text.tsx`. Cover that the flow name and Workflow icon render for a mocked `/flows/:id` response, that the link points to `/flows/flow/$id` with the flow id, and that the fallback shows while pending. Follow `flow-menu.test.tsx` in the detail folder, and assert on rendered output.

findings.title: Skeleton fallback dropped and its import left unused
findings.body:
The description says a Skeleton fallback is used, and `FlowLink` does `<Suspense fallback={<Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />}>`. Here the `Skeleton` import on line 6 is never used, and the Suspense on line 14 has no fallback. The file will likely fail lint for an unused import. While the query is pending, the component renders nothing, so the layout shifts when the name appears.

::diff{file="ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/flow-icon-text.tsx" lines="6-14"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/flow-icon-text.tsx`, the Suspense on line 14 has no fallback, while the Skeleton import on line 6 is unused. Add a fallback of `<Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />` to that Suspense, matching `FlowLink` in `flow-link.tsx` line 14. This keeps the import used and removes the layout shift.

findings.title: Story builds an unused QueryClient and a router on every render
findings.body:
Line 32 of the story passes `context: { queryClient: new QueryClient() }` to `createRouter`, but nothing reads that context. The component gets its client from the `QueryClientProvider` on line 43. `createTestRouter` also runs inside the decorator, so a new router is built on every render. The repo's `routerDecorator` from `@/storybook/utils` covers this case, as `flow-menu.stories.tsx` shows.

::diff{file="ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/flow-icon-text.stories.tsx" lines="29-33"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/flow-icon-text.stories.tsx`, remove the unused `context: { queryClient: new QueryClient() }` on line 32. Replace the hand-built router with the shared `routerDecorator` from `@/storybook/utils`, as `flow-menu.stories.tsx` does. Keep the `flow-123` default story.

findings.title: Component reuses the shared query, route, and icon from FlowLink
findings.body: The component reuses `buildFLowDetailsQuery`, the `/flows/flow/$id` route with `params.id = flow.id`, and the `Workflow` icon, all of which `FlowLink` also uses. It adds no new data-layer concepts, and the query cache is shared with the existing callers. The barrel `index.ts` exports only `FlowIconText`, which matches the folder convention.

architecture.overview:
The existing flow link UI is FlowLink in ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-link.tsx. It wraps a Suspense boundary around an implementation that calls useSuspenseQuery(buildFLowDetailsQuery(flowId)) from @/api/flows, then renders a literal Flow label followed by a TanStack Link to /flows/flow/$id with a Workflow icon and the flow name.

The PR adds FlowIconText as a sibling for contexts that only want the icon and name. It keeps the same query, route, and icon, and drops the Flow prefix. Its own Suspense boundary has no fallback, so the loading state renders nothing. The story wires a standalone router and QueryClient for Storybook. Nothing in the repo consumes the new module yet.
steps: Entry point: a consumer passes a flowId to FlowIconText (flow-icon-text.tsx, line 12). It wraps its implementation in a Suspense boundary with no fallback (line 14).
Data fetch: FlowIconTextImplementation (line 20) calls useSuspenseQuery(buildFLowDetailsQuery(flowId)) (line 21). This is the same query builder FlowLink uses, so cache entries are shared.
Render: it renders a TanStack Link to /flows/flow/$id with params.id = flow.id (lines 24-28), containing a Workflow icon and flow.name (lines 29-30).
Storybook: flow-icon-text.stories.tsx builds its own root route and router and wraps the component in a QueryClientProvider (lines 20-47).
Gap: the PR description claims unit tests, but the diff adds no test file, so loading state, link target, and rendered name are untested.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #20030 - Add FlowIconText component for UI v2 migration

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds a FlowIconText component under ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/. It fetches a flow by ID and renders the flow's Workflow icon and name as a link to /flows/flow/$id, without the Flow label that FlowLink renders. It reuses FlowLink's query builder, icon, and route, so the data path is sound. The diff adds the component, a Storybook story, and an index.ts barrel.

Three problems stand out. The PR description and checklist say a flow-icon-text.test.tsx was added, but no test file is in the diff or on the head branch. The component drops the Skeleton fallback that the description and FlowLink use, which leaves the Skeleton import unused and renders nothing while loading. The story also carries dead and redundant router setup. None of these break runtime behaviour, but the first two should be fixed before merge.
structured_output.verdictRationale:
The checklist claims unit tests that do not exist, so the new component ships with no coverage. The unused Skeleton import and missing loading fallback diverge from FlowLink and likely fail lint. The story issues are cosmetic. The fixes are small.</verdictRationale>
</invoke>
